title: LibKa0s — Autocomplete hooks, callbacks and options
cluster_summary: All five findings concern LibKa0s/WidgetsAutocomplete.lua (minor 1), and all fixes belong to the C-03 pass on LibKa0s. Neither adopter (LootHistory, BankLedger) reaches any of these paths today. The one item worth doing is LK-R-02: the API doc never says the box's scripts must be set before lib.Autocomplete, and hooked[box] means a later SetScript silently kills the list. The doc fix is required. A generation-guarded re-hook is optional hardening, and the testkit mock already drops hooks on SetScript. LK-R-05 is refuted, because Core.lua:675 states the library's policy that host callbacks are not pcall'd. The rest are cheap optional tidy-ups in the same file.

verdicts.assessment: The mechanism is real. hookBox (WidgetsAutocomplete.lua:345-349) never re-hooks, so a later SetScript drops the hooks and they stay dropped. The API doc does not promise that re-calling recovers the box (docs:1216-1219 say 'hooked once per box'), but it also never states the set-scripts-first precondition. testkit/mock_base.lua:155 SetScript already overwrites HookScript wrappers, so the mock needs no change. Both adopters set their scripts first, so the severity is low.
verdicts.remediation: C-03: add to the 'Hooks, never scripts' bullet in docs/api/Widgets that the host must set the box's scripts before calling Autocomplete, because a later SetScript on a hooked script drops the hooks and re-calling does not reinstall them. Optional: re-hook on each call behind a per-box generation so that older wrappers do nothing, with tests that a re-call after SetScript works and that a re-call without SetScript does not double-dispatch. No mock or testkit change.

verdicts.assessment: The library's convention is not to pcall host callbacks. Core.lua:675 says so, and dd.onSelect at Widgets.lua:171 is called unprotected. Only tooltipPlace is pcall'd, because it has a defined fallback. A raising provider reaches geterrorhandler() with a stack trace that names the host's function, so wrapping it would only hide host bugs.

The comment is wrong only for `owners`, whose value (handle.__box) strongly references the key. Lua 5.1 has no ephemerons, so that entry stays until Release. `hooked` holds true, so its entries really can be collected. Client frames are never collected anyway, so there is no runtime effect.
verdicts.remediation: C-03, folded into the LK-R-02 edit: change the comment at :67-68 to say that `owners` entries persist until Release or replacement because the handle references its box, and that this is harmless since frames live for the whole session.

verdicts.assessment: positive() accepts fractional values, so maxRows=2.5 draws 2 rows in a list 2.5 rows tall. Nothing raises. Both adopters pass the integer 8, so this is input hygiene only.
verdicts.remediation: C-03: floor maxRows after the >0 check, and fall back to AC.MAX_ROWS when the floored value is below 1.

verdicts.assessment: skin() does call SetBackdrop on every render, but render runs at most once per debounce of at least 0.15s, and the finding admits the cost was never measured. This is a tidy-up, not a performance defect.
verdicts.remediation: Optional in C-03: call SetBackdrop once in ensureList, or hoist the table to a constant, and keep the per-show SetBackdropColor and SetBackdropBorderColor calls so a host restyle still carries over.
